content.value_statement: Angular teams need consistent role and ability checks across routes, components, and data access. This skill shows practical @delon/acl patterns for guards, UI visibility, and server-side validation.
actual_capabilities: Explains ACLService setup for roles, abilities, and permission modes.
Shows *aclIf and Angular @if patterns for conditional UI.
Provides route guard examples for role and ability checks.
Maps blueprint membership roles to task and blueprint permissions.
Documents Firestore security rules as required server-side enforcement.
limitations: Contains guidance only; it does not run code or install dependencies.
Client-side UI checks are not a substitute for backend authorization.
Project-specific services like AuthService must be adapted.

use_cases.title: Add Role Guards
use_cases.description: Protect admin, task creation, and blueprint editing routes with @delon/acl guard patterns.

use_cases.title: Standardize Permission Models
use_cases.description: Define owner, admin, member, and viewer abilities for blueprint-based workflows.

use_cases.title: Review Access Control Coverage
use_cases.description: Compare UI checks, route guards, and Firestore rules before release.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Basic ACL
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the delon-acl skill to show how to initialize ACLService with admin and user roles in an Angular component.

prompt_templates.title: Add Conditional UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the delon-acl skill to hide create, edit, and delete buttons with *aclIf and Angular @if patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Design Route Guards
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the delon-acl skill to create route guards for admin access, task creation, and blueprint editing in Angular.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Permission Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the delon-acl skill to review a blueprint permission model, including roles, abilities, route guards, UI checks, and Firestore rules.

output_examples.input: Need to protect an admin route.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends an admin guard that checks the admin role and redirects unauthorized users to a 403 route.

output_examples.input: Need task buttons to respect permissions.
output_examples.output: It suggests ACL checks for create, edit, and delete buttons while keeping backend rules authoritative.
It maps membership roles to abilities and highlights assigned-user checks for task editing.

best_practices: Initialize ACL after authentication before protected routes render.
Use route guards and backend rules for every protected action.
Keep roles broad and abilities specific to each feature action.
anti_patterns: Relying only on hidden buttons to protect sensitive actions.
Hardcoding role names across many components instead of using ACLService.
Granting broad roles when a narrow ability check is sufficient.

faq.question: Does this skill install @delon/acl?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples for projects that install the package separately.

faq.question: Can it enforce security by itself?
faq.answer: No. Client ACL must be paired with server-side authorization or Firestore security rules.

faq.question: Which framework does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Angular, ng-alain, and @delon/acl version 20.1.0 examples.

faq.question: Does it support route guards?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes role-based, ability-based, and combined guard patterns.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The content is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is it specific to ng-events?
faq.answer: Many examples use ng-events blueprint and task workflows, but the patterns can be adapted.
